feature: Destruction effects (DE) on the VFX Bench: the 11 effects - material-matched debris (wood, stone, metal, cloth, glass; small and large) and a lit light's death
version: the install after anim ce6e074 + the game session's trigger
setup: The install named in Version (a development build: the dev layer on, as for the VFX Bench). Start the game and load any game with a character in play; in game chat type !vfxexport (the bench's library written again, with the game's chunk models these effects throw). Then start the VFX Bench (nwn5e-tools vfx_bench\vfx_bench.bat); if it was already open, press Reload.
do: 1. In the bench press Open, pick the nwn5e tab and open n5_db_wood_s; watch the stage, Restart two or three times, turn the camera round it. Do the same for n5_db_wood_l, n5_db_stone_s, n5_db_stone_l, n5_db_metal_s, n5_db_metal_l, n5_db_cloth_s, n5_db_cloth_l, n5_db_glass_s, n5_db_glass_l and n5_db_light. 2. In the Game tab find rows 2248 to 2258 (NWN5E_DEBRIS_WOOD_S to NWN5E_LIGHT_DEATH) and open two of them. 3. Open n5_db_metal_l, then n5_db_light, and press Play in game for each, watching your character.
expect: 1: each plays once and is gone by its end (3.5 to 5 s), nothing left behind. Wood: brown dust and planks flying out and bouncing. Stone: grey-brown dust, stone chunks and small rocks that lie about 4 s. Metal: grey dust, small dark pieces and bright specks that streak, fall and bounce. Cloth: pale dust and one (small) or three (large) of the same small dark pieces as scraps - one game chunk for both: metal is told by its sparks and grey dust. Glass: small shards thrown wide, white streaks turning ice blue, a faint blue-grey puff (large: bigger glass too). Each large one throws more, from higher (to about 1.3 m). n5_db_light: orange sparks burst, embers drift up and shrink, a grey smoke column rises past a metre, a warm light comes on at once and fades to dark by about 1.5 s. The pieces are the game's, not cubes. 2: the same effects under those labels. 3: in game the same look, at your feet. Say which looks wrong: cubes, a colour off for its material, something left behind, the light late or not fading.
note: owner (0.99.110): "DE-1 still nothing" - bench Play in game of the n5_db_* one-shots; the shipped models are identical and break fine in game (DE-2b) - the bench applies them on you (row 1600, instant), a break at a location

feature: Destruction effects (DE) in game: broken pieces - their own debris unchanged, material debris where a piece has none, and a lit light's embers, smoke and fading glow
version: the install after anim ce6e074 + the game session's trigger
setup: The install named in Version (with the game session's trigger in its death hook). Load your save of the Prelude ("familiartest"); in game chat type !test level2wizard (a Wizard 5: Fire Bolt and Shatter prepared). In the Training Halls (m0q1b): the trainers' sign "Flag / Pennant / Banner - 3" (a cloth banner), the bones on the floor, a bolt of cloth or a hay bale, the wagon wheel, the urn and the lit braziers. In the Academy (m0q1d): a bench (pew), the lectern and the lit candelabra.
do: Lit lights first, each with Fire Bolt alone - fire doesn't put a light out; any other hit does, and Shatter puts out every light in its sphere: 1. In m0q1b Fire Bolt a lit brazier, again until it breaks. 2. In m0q1d Fire Bolt the lit candelabra until it breaks. Then the rest with Shatter (cast again if one survives; a weapon reaches only clickable pieces): 3. In m0q1b the banner-sign, the bones, a bolt of cloth or hay bale, and the wagon wheel. 4. The urn. 5. In m0q1d a bench and the lectern. 6. Another lit brazier: hit it once with a weapon (it goes out), then break it with Fire Bolt or Shatter.
expect: 1: the brazier throws its own metal and stone chunks and smoke, and where its fire was: orange sparks, embers drifting up, a grey smoke column rising past a metre and a warm glow dimming to nothing in about 1.5 s - not a light that just goes out. 2: the candelabra its own debris, with the embers, smoke and glow up at its candles (about 1.9 m). 3: each throws debris fitting its material: the banner, cloth and hay pale dust and small dark scraps; the bones small planks and brown dust (over their own small smoke); the wagon wheel planks and dust from higher up. Each plays out (about 3.5 s) after the piece is gone. 4: the urn its own stone chunks and dust, nothing added. 5: the bench and the lectern their own wooden debris (the lectern its fountain), nothing added. 6: a light put out before it breaks gives only its own debris - no embers, smoke or glow. Say which: no debris where a piece had none, debris doubled, the wrong material, embers or glow missing (or on a put-out light), or cut off.
note: owner (0.99.106): "destroying a candelabra/brazier with fire bolts doesn't seem to get rid of their light source" - retest DE-2b (0.99.107)
